4063198.background: Special election for Rubio's former seat, held by appointed Republican Ashley Moody. Miami-Dade, once a reliable Democratic county, swung hard right: DeSantis won it in 2022 and Trump carried it by about 11 points in 2024, driven by Hispanic voters. Democrats hope a midterm backlash reverses part of that.

actors.name: Ashley Moody (R nominee)
actors.public: Appointed senator, former attorney general, Trump-endorsed, strong fundraising and statewide name recognition; Florida GOP has a large voter-registration advantage.
actors.private: Wants a comfortable statewide margin; Miami-Dade matters for the margin but is not essential to her. Exposed if Hispanic voters sour on tariffs or deportations.

actors.name: Democratic nominee
actors.public: Lower-profile candidate with limited money in an expensive state; national Democrats have treated Florida as a low priority.
actors.private: Needs Cuban, Venezuelan and other Hispanic voters to swing back over immigration enforcement and TPS/parole cancellations; probably lacks the resources to drive that.

actors.name: Miami-Dade Hispanic electorate
actors.public: Moved sharply toward Republicans from 2016 to 2024.
actors.private: Some 2025-26 polling and local results showed softening over deportations and the economy; turnout in a midterm will be decisive.

events.name: Major immigration-enforcement controversy hitting South Florida Hispanic communities
National Democratic wave environment of 5+ points on the generic ballot

4063831.background: Open Michigan Senate seat after Gary Peters retired. Republican Mike Rogers faces the Democratic nominee chosen in the August 2026 primary (McMorrow, Stevens or El-Sayed). Genesee County (Flint) is historically Democratic but has trended right; Harris won it only narrowly in 2024 and Slotkin narrowly carried it.

actors.name: Democratic nominee
actors.public: Winner of a contested primary among Mallory McMorrow, Haley Stevens and Abdul El-Sayed; backed by national party money.
actors.private: Needs strong Black turnout in Flint and to hold union whites; a bruising primary could dent enthusiasm.

actors.name: Mike Rogers (R)
actors.public: Former congressman, lost to Slotkin by about 0.3 points in 2024, Trump-endorsed, cleared the GOP field.
actors.private: Targets working-class and union voters in places like Genesee; tariffs and auto-sector pain cut both ways.

actors.name: Genesee County electorate
actors.public: Unionized, Flint has a large Black population; drifting Republican in recent presidential cycles.
actors.private: Midterm turnout drop in Flint hurts Democrats; a backlash against the president helps them.

events.name: Auto industry layoffs or tariff shock in mid-Michigan

4063889.background: Open Michigan Senate seat (Peters retired); Republican Mike Rogers versus the Democratic primary winner. Oakland County, suburban Detroit, has become solidly Democratic: Biden and Harris won it by roughly 10-14 points, and Whitmer and Slotkin carried it comfortably.

actors.name: Democratic nominee
actors.public: McMorrow and Stevens are both Oakland-area figures with local bases; strong suburban fundraising.
actors.private: Needs to run up the margin in Oakland to offset rural losses; a candidate from the county is helped.

actors.name: Mike Rogers (R)
actors.public: Former congressman, came within 0.3 points statewide in 2024; Trump-endorsed.
actors.private: Aims to cut losses among college-educated suburbanites rather than win Oakland.

actors.name: Oakland suburban electorate
actors.public: Highly educated, high-turnout, trending Democratic since 2016.
actors.private: Midterms with a Republican president tend to deepen anti-incumbent suburban swing.

events.name: Major scandal involving the Democratic nominee

4063957.background: Texas Senate race after a bitter Republican primary among John Cornyn, Ken Paxton and Wesley Hunt, against a Democrat (James Talarico or Jasmine Crockett). Tarrant County (Fort Worth) is the most Republican of Texas's big urban counties; Beto narrowly won it in 2018, Biden won it narrowly in 2020, Trump won by about 5 in 2024.

actors.name: Republican nominee
actors.public: Either Cornyn (establishment, heavy fundraising) or Paxton (Trump-aligned, scandal-laden); party has a structural edge statewide.
actors.private: A Paxton nomination risks suburban defections in Tarrant; a Cornyn nomination may depress base enthusiasm.

actors.name: Democratic nominee
actors.public: Talarico or Crockett, with strong grassroots fundraising and national attention.
actors.private: Talarico plays better with suburban moderates; Crockett energizes the base but alienates swing voters. Tarrant is a key test.

actors.name: Tarrant suburban electorate
actors.public: Swing county that moved back to Republicans in 2022 and 2024.
actors.private: Hispanic voters swung right in 2024; a midterm backlash and a Paxton nominee could reverse it.

events.name: Ken Paxton is the Republican nominee

4063993.background: Texas Senate general election after a contested Republican primary (Cornyn, Paxton, Hunt) against a Democrat such as Talarico or Crockett. Collin County, a fast-growing Dallas suburb, has shifted left but remains Republican: Trump won it by about 9-10 points in 2024; Beto lost it by roughly 6 in 2018.

actors.name: Republican nominee
actors.public: Cornyn or Paxton (Paxton lives in Collin and was its state senator); strong party infrastructure.
actors.private: Paxton has home-county ties but scandals cost him college-educated voters; Cornyn has broader suburban appeal.

actors.name: Democratic nominee
actors.public: Talarico or Crockett, well-funded through online donations.
actors.private: Winning Collin requires a large anti-Trump suburban swing beyond 2018 levels.

actors.name: Collin County electorate
actors.public: Affluent, educated, diverse, with many Asian American and new-resident voters; trending left slowly.
actors.private: Many traditional Republicans could split tickets against a scandal-plagued nominee.

events.name: Ken Paxton is the Republican nominee

4064440.background: Nevada governor race: Republican incumbent Joe Lombardo against Democratic Attorney General Aaron Ford. Washoe County (Reno) is the classic swing county; Lombardo won it in 2022, Biden won it in 2020, and Trump narrowly carried it or tied in 2024.

actors.name: Joe Lombardo (R, incumbent)
actors.public: First-term governor, record veto count, moderate image, good approval; won 2022 by about 1.5 points.
actors.private: Will run on independence from Trump; Washoe moderates are central to his coalition.

actors.name: Aaron Ford (D)
actors.public: Two-term attorney general, cleared most of the primary field, backed by state party and unions.
actors.private: Needs to nationalize the race against Trump; weaker personal brand in northern Nevada than in Clark.

actors.name: Washoe County electorate
actors.public: Nearly evenly split, large nonpartisan registration share.
actors.private: Ticket-splitting likely; incumbency and midterm anti-presidential swing pull in opposite directions.

events.name: Scandal or major misstep by either nominee

4064647.background: Arizona governor race: Democratic incumbent Katie Hobbs against the Republican nominee from a primary among Andy Biggs, Karrin Taylor Robson (both Trump-endorsed at one point) and David Schweikert. Maricopa holds about 60% of the vote; Hobbs narrowly won it in 2022, Trump won it in 2024.

actors.name: Katie Hobbs (D, incumbent)
actors.public: First-term governor, record vetoes, large war chest; won 2022 by under 1 point.
actors.private: Banking on Republican nominee being too extreme for Maricopa suburbs; approval only middling.

actors.name: Republican nominee
actors.public: Likely Andy Biggs, a hard-right Freedom Caucus figure, or a more establishment alternative; Trump-endorsed.
actors.private: Biggs mobilizes the base but risks repeating Kari Lake's suburban losses.

actors.name: Maricopa County electorate
actors.public: Large swing suburban county; Republicans hold a registration edge.
actors.private: Independents and moderate Republicans decide it; midterm environment favors the out-party.

events.name: Andy Biggs is the Republican nominee

4096418.background: Russian State Duma election set for 18-20 September 2026: 225 list seats (5% threshold) and 225 single-member districts. The Greens won 0.9% and no seats in 2021. Elections are tightly managed by the Kremlin; minor parties occasionally get a district seat when United Russia stands aside.

actors.name: Presidential Administration / Kremlin
actors.public: Manages the outcome through candidate registration, media and administrative resources; United Russia expected to dominate.
actors.private: Sometimes allocates single-member districts to loyal minor parties as rewards; unclear whether the Greens are favored this cycle.

actors.name: Russian Ecological Party The Greens
actors.public: Small, systemic, loyal party polling around 1%.
actors.private: Realistic path is only a district deal with United Russia standing down; no prospect of passing 5%.

actors.name: Central Election Commission
actors.public: Certifies results; multi-day voting and online voting.
actors.private: Will reflect the Kremlin's preferred distribution.

events.name: United Russia withdraws its candidate in a district for a Greens nominee

4096539.background: Russian Duma election 18-20 September 2026. LDPR, led by Leonid Slutsky since Zhirinovsky's death in 2022, won 21 seats in 2021 (7.5%). Some 2025-26 polls put LDPR near second place, around 10-12%, but 95 seats would require a huge jump in managed elections.

actors.name: Kremlin / Presidential Administration
actors.public: Arranges seat distribution; United Russia expected to keep a constitutional majority.
actors.private: May boost LDPR modestly at the communists' expense, but has no interest in a large LDPR bloc.

actors.name: LDPR (Leonid Slutsky)
actors.public: Loyal, nationalist, pro-war party; claims to be the main opposition.
actors.private: Realistic aim is second place and perhaps 30-60 seats with district deals.

actors.name: United Russia
actors.public: Ruling party, wins most single-member districts.
actors.private: Will cede only a few districts to allies.

events.name: Kremlin-engineered surge giving LDPR second place

4096543.background: Russian Duma election 18-20 September 2026. New People, a Kremlin-tolerated liberal-business party led by Alexei Nechaev, entered the Duma in 2021 with 5.3% and 15 seats. Polls in 2025-26 put it around 5-8%. Reaching 35 seats would require roughly doubling its 2021 performance.

actors.name: Kremlin / Presidential Administration
actors.public: Controls registration and outcome management.
actors.private: Uses New People as a safety valve for urban, younger voters; unlikely to let it grow large.

actors.name: New People (Alexei Nechaev)
actors.public: Pro-system party focused on business and urban issues; modest regional gains since 2021.
actors.private: Aims to clear 5% again and win a few districts; 35+ seats would be an outlier.

actors.name: Central Election Commission
actors.public: Certifies results.
actors.private: Will follow managed seat distribution.

events.name: New People fails to cross the 5% threshold

4118938.background: Russia-Ukraine direct talks occurred in Istanbul (May-July 2025) and US-brokered trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi and Geneva in early 2026, without a settlement. US envoys Witkoff and Kushner shuttle between sides. Fighting continues; territory in Donetsk remains the core sticking point.

actors.name: Vladimir Putin / Kremlin
actors.public: Demands all of Donbas, Ukrainian neutrality, limits on Ukraine's army; accepts talks in principle.
actors.private: Willing to meet to appear constructive to Trump while continuing offensives; not near accepting a ceasefire on current lines.

actors.name: Volodymyr Zelensky / Kyiv
actors.public: Ready for ceasefire on current lines and security guarantees; refuses to cede unoccupied territory.
actors.private: Will attend any US-brokered talks to keep Washington onside.

actors.name: Trump administration (Witkoff, Kushner, Rubio)
actors.public: Pushes for a deal, hosts or brokers meetings, uses sanctions and aid as leverage.
actors.private: Wants a visible diplomatic win before the midterms; may convene trilateral meetings frequently.

events.name: New trilateral round convened by US mediators

4148956.background: After the 2026 US-Iran conflict, the US imposed a naval blockade on Iranian shipping; Trump announced its reinstatement on 13 July 2026. A Xi Jinping visit to the US was expected later in 2026 following Trump's spring Beijing trip. China is Iran's main oil customer.

actors.name: Donald Trump / White House
actors.public: Uses the blockade as leverage for a nuclear and missile deal with Iran.
actors.private: Could suspend the blockade suddenly as part of a deal or as a gesture to China ahead of trade talks; unpredictable timing.

actors.name: Iranian leadership
actors.public: Rejects talks under pressure, threatens Hormuz disruption.
actors.private: Economic pain is severe; may accept indirect talks via Oman or Qatar for blockade relief.

actors.name: Xi Jinping / Beijing
actors.public: Opposes the blockade, seeks trade deal with the US.
actors.private: May press for relief before visiting; the visit date itself determines the window.

events.name: Xi visit to US occurs within the period

4155307.background: CNN House exit poll. In 2024 young men swung strongly to Trump; exit polls showed Trump winning men 18-29 by double digits. In the 2018 midterm Democrats won young voters broadly. 2026 polling suggested young men soured on Trump, while CNN may report only 18-29 if 18-24 men are unavailable.

actors.name: Young male electorate
actors.public: Shifted rightward in 2024, driven by economy and online culture.
actors.private: Low-turnout group; disapproval of Trump grew during 2025-26 over the economy and prices.

actors.name: Democratic Party
actors.public: Invested in podcast and online outreach to young men after 2024.
actors.private: Expects a midterm swing to help but young men remain its weakest young subgroup.

actors.name: Republican Party
actors.public: Relies on influencer ecosystem and Trump-era messaging.
actors.private: Without Trump on the ballot, turnout of low-propensity young men may drop.

actors.name: Exit poll consortium (CNN/Edison)
actors.public: Reports subgroups; small samples for 18-24 men.
actors.private: Crosstab may be noisy or presented as 18-29.

events.name: National Democratic wave of 5+ points in House vote

4155318.background: CNN House exit poll. Latino men swung sharply to Trump in 2024 (exit polls about 55-43 Trump). In the 2018 midterm Democrats won Latinos by about 40 points. 2025 elections in New Jersey, Virginia and elsewhere showed Latino voters swinging back to Democrats.

actors.name: Latino male electorate
actors.public: Moved right in 2024 over economy and inflation.
actors.private: Deportation raids and price pressures reportedly reversed much of the shift in 2025 polling.

actors.name: Democratic Party
actors.public: Campaigns on cost of living and immigration enforcement excesses.
actors.private: Expects significant recovery but uncertain if it returns to 2018 levels.

actors.name: Republican Party
actors.public: Touts 2024 gains and border security.
actors.private: Fears losing Latino gains without Trump on ballot.

4188128.background: Pete Hegseth has led the Pentagon (also styled Department of War since 2025) since January 2025, surviving Signalgate, staff purges, the boat-strike controversy and criticism over the Iran campaign. Trump has consistently backed him publicly.

actors.name: Donald Trump
actors.public: Repeatedly defends Hegseth.
actors.private: Values loyalty; would drop him only after a damaging scandal or if he became a political liability before midterms.

actors.name: Pete Hegseth
actors.public: Combative, loyal, has reshaped Pentagon leadership.
actors.private: No sign of wanting to leave; could seek a political run later.

actors.name: Congressional Republicans
actors.public: Mostly supportive, a few senators critical.
actors.private: Would not force removal before midterms.

events.name: Major new Hegseth scandal or inspector-general finding

4188133.background: Pete Hegseth has been Defense (War) Secretary since January 2025, surviving Signalgate, purges of senior officers, boat-strike legal controversy and war-related criticism. Trump continues to back him; the midterms make a pre-election shake-up less attractive.

actors.name: Donald Trump
actors.public: Publicly supportive of Hegseth.
actors.private: Typically reshuffles after elections rather than before; would act only on a severe scandal.

actors.name: Pete Hegseth
actors.public: Loyal, combative, popular with MAGA base.
actors.private: Intends to stay; possible future political ambitions.

actors.name: Senate Republicans
actors.public: Largely back him.
actors.private: Unlikely to pressure before November.

4196367.background: Tasmanian local government elections, postal ballots closing late October 2026. Alison Jarman has been Devonport mayor since 2022 (previously deputy and councillor); mayors are elected directly by first-past-the-post. Incumbent mayors in Tasmania are usually re-elected.

actors.name: Alison Jarman
actors.public: Incumbent mayor, well known locally, has run Devonport through the Living City developments.
actors.private: Likely to recontest; vulnerability comes from rates rises or council controversy.

actors.name: Challenger councillors
actors.public: Other councillors may stand for mayor.
actors.private: A strong, well-known challenger is required to unseat an incumbent.

actors.name: Devonport ratepayers
actors.public: Compulsory postal voting does not apply; turnout around 55-60%.
actors.private: Name recognition dominates.

4196434.background: Tasmanian local elections in October 2026, postal voting. Cheryl Fuller became Central Coast mayor in 2022 after serving as deputy; mayor is directly elected. Incumbents usually win in Tasmanian councils.

actors.name: Cheryl Fuller
actors.public: Incumbent mayor with long council service.
actors.private: Likely to run again; age or fatigue could lead to retirement.

actors.name: Challengers
actors.public: Other councillors or community figures may nominate.
actors.private: Need local profile to beat an incumbent.

actors.name: Central Coast voters
actors.public: Voluntary postal ballot.
actors.private: Respond to rates and service issues.

events.name: Strong challenger such as the deputy mayor runs

4196736.background: Huon Valley council was suspended and administered in 2016-18; Sally Doyle was elected mayor in 2022. Tasmanian council elections in October 2026, direct mayoral vote by postal ballot.

actors.name: Sally Doyle
actors.public: Incumbent mayor, first term.
actors.private: Likely to recontest; council tensions in Huon Valley have history.

actors.name: Challengers
actors.public: Councillors or former mayors may run.
actors.private: Fragmented field helps the incumbent.

actors.name: Huon Valley voters
actors.public: Postal voting, moderate turnout.
actors.private: Local planning and growth issues dominate.

4196860.background: Latrobe Council, Tasmania. Peter Freshney has been mayor for many years and is a long-serving local figure. Tasmanian council elections in October 2026, direct mayoral vote by postal ballot.

actors.name: Peter Freshney
actors.public: Long-serving incumbent mayor with strong local recognition.
actors.private: Age could prompt retirement; if he runs, usually favored.

actors.name: Challengers
actors.public: Possible councillor challengers.
actors.private: Unseating a long-term incumbent is difficult.

actors.name: Latrobe voters
actors.public: Small rural-town electorate.
actors.private: Personal familiarity dominates.

4198830.background: Brazil's first round is 4 October 2026. Renan Santos, MBL co-founder, is the presidential candidate of the new Missão party. Broadcasters must invite candidates of parties with at least five federal legislators; Missão is new with very little congressional representation, so inclusion depends on broadcaster discretion.

actors.name: Renan Santos / Missão
actors.public: Outsider right-wing candidate, strong online following, polling low single digits.
actors.private: Will fight hard, including legally, for debate invitations.

actors.name: Broadcasters (Globo, Band, SBT, Record, CNN Brasil)
actors.public: Follow legal minimum invitation rule; may invite others by agreement.
actors.private: Other campaigns can veto extra invitees; smaller outlets more flexible.

actors.name: Major campaigns (Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro / Tarcísio side)
actors.public: Negotiate debate rules.
actors.private: May resist adding a disruptive outsider.

events.name: Missão gains enough congressional members for mandatory invitation
A broadcaster invites Santos at its discretion

4199057.background: Israeli Knesset election expected 27 October 2026. Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announced a joint list called Together (Beyachad) in 2026. Bennett's party alone polled around 18-24 seats in 2025; Yesh Atid had fallen to single digits. Combined list polling is uncertain.

actors.name: Naftali Bennett
actors.public: Leading opposition figure for premiership; polled strongly through 2025.
actors.private: Wants largest-party status to form a government; merger aims to consolidate the center-right/center bloc.

actors.name: Yair Lapid
actors.public: Opposition leader, Yesh Atid declining in polls.
actors.private: Accepts junior role to remain relevant.

actors.name: Benjamin Netanyahu / Likud
actors.public: Seeks re-election, attacks opposition merger.
actors.private: Will campaign on security; timing of election could shift.

actors.name: Other opposition parties (Eisenkot, Lieberman, Democrats)
actors.public: Compete for the same anti-Netanyahu voters.
actors.private: Further mergers could change Together's count.

4199214.background: CNN House exit poll. Republicans won white women in most recent elections: Trump about 53% in 2024; in the 2018 midterm wave, exit polls showed white women split nearly evenly (about 49-49). 2025 off-year results showed sharp swings among women toward Democrats.

actors.name: White female electorate
actors.public: Leaned Republican, with large education divide.
actors.private: College-educated white women strongly Democratic; non-college strongly Republican.

actors.name: Democratic Party
actors.public: Campaigns on abortion, health care, costs.
actors.private: Needs a 2018-level environment or better to win the group.

actors.name: Republican Party
actors.public: Relies on non-college white women.
actors.private: Turnout drop among irregular voters in midterms is a risk.

4202006.background: Göttingen mayoral election 13 September 2026, runoff 27 September. Incumbent Petra Broistedt (independent, backed by Greens and CDU) was elected in 2021. Göttingen is a left-leaning university city; Florian Dinger is among the challengers.

actors.name: Petra Broistedt
actors.public: Incumbent mayor since 2021 with Greens/CDU backing.
actors.private: Incumbency advantage; record on finances and housing open to attack.

actors.name: Florian Dinger
actors.public: Challenger; party backing and profile not well known to me.
actors.private: Needs to reach runoff and consolidate other parties' voters.

actors.name: SPD and other parties
actors.public: SPD historically strong in Göttingen.
actors.private: Runoff endorsements decide outcome.

4221710.background: Arizona Attorney General: Democrat Kris Mayes, who won in 2022 by 280 votes, seeks re-election. Republicans include state Senate President Warren Petersen and Rodney Glassman. Mayes prosecuted fake electors and has been active against Trump policies.

actors.name: Kris Mayes (D, incumbent)
actors.public: High-profile incumbent, aggressive litigation against Trump administration.
actors.private: Benefits from incumbency and a midterm environment; Mayes faced some ethics criticism.

actors.name: Republican nominee
actors.public: Likely Warren Petersen, establishment conservative legislator.
actors.private: Needs Republican registration edge to carry the race.

actors.name: Arizona electorate
actors.public: Republicans hold registration edge; Trump won 2024 by 5.5.
actors.private: Midterm with Republican president favors Democrats statewide.

4221855.background: Florida Attorney General: Republican James Uthmeier, appointed by DeSantis in 2025 after Moody went to the Senate, seeks a full term. Florida Republicans have a voter-registration lead above one million and won statewide by large margins in 2022 and 2024.

actors.name: James Uthmeier (R)
actors.public: DeSantis ally, appointed incumbent; involved in Hope Florida controversy.
actors.private: Scandal exposure small relative to partisan advantage.

actors.name: Democratic nominee
actors.public: Low-profile, under-funded.
actors.private: Needs scandal plus wave.

actors.name: Florida electorate
actors.public: Strongly Republican since 2022.
actors.private: Midterm backlash could narrow margins.

events.name: Hope Florida investigation escalates to charges

4222149.background: Minnesota Attorney General: Democrat Keith Ellison seeks a third term; he won by under 1 point in 2022. Minnesota's political scene was shaken by the 2025 assassination of Melissa Hortman and fraud scandals; Gov. Walz dropped re-election bid.

actors.name: Keith Ellison (DFL)
actors.public: Two-term incumbent, progressive, high-profile litigant against Trump policies.
actors.private: Fraud scandals (Feeding Our Future) could be used against him.

actors.name: Republican nominee

actors.private: Needs Ellison-specific weakness to overcome DFL lean.

actors.public: Leans DFL; no Republican statewide win since 2006.
actors.private: Midterm environment favours DFL.

4222171.background: New York Attorney General: Democrat Letitia James seeks a third term. She was indicted for mortgage fraud in 2025 but the case was dismissed. New York is strongly Democratic; no Republican has won statewide since 2002.

actors.name: Letitia James (D)
actors.public: High-profile Trump antagonist, strong Democratic base.
actors.private: Legal case could resurface; otherwise secure.

actors.name: Republican nominee
actors.public: Low-name-recognition challenger.
actors.private: Needs a scandal and low Democratic turnout.

actors.name: New York electorate
actors.public: Democratic by about 10-20 points statewide.
actors.private: 2022 saw a red shift, but midterm with Republican president favors Democrats.

4222345.background: Indiana Secretary of State: Republican incumbent Diego Morales has faced controversy over travel and staffing. Indiana is strongly Republican; Democrats have not won a statewide race since 2012.

actors.name: Republican nominee (Diego Morales or convention rival)
actors.public: Party nominated at convention; strong partisan base.
actors.private: Morales controversies could cost some votes but not the race.

actors.name: Democratic nominee
actors.public: Low-profile candidate.
actors.private: Hopes for scandal-driven crossover votes.

actors.name: Indiana electorate
actors.public: Republican by 15-20 points.
actors.private: Midterm environment unlikely to flip.

4222441.background: Texas Lieutenant Governor: Republican Dan Patrick, in office since 2015, seeks a fourth term. Democrats nominated a lower-profile candidate (such as Vikki Goodwin). Republicans have won every Texas statewide race since 1994.

actors.name: Dan Patrick (R)
actors.public: Powerful incumbent, strong fundraising, Trump ally.
actors.private: Age and health are limited risks; secure seat.

actors.name: Democratic nominee
actors.public: Low-profile state legislator or activist.
actors.private: Needs exceptional wave and turnout.
